newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JONES CLINCHES FIRST TITLE BY WIDTH OF VEST.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JONES CLINCHES FIRST TITLE BY WIDTH OF VEST.

text.p: American champion Marion Jones ushered in a new era in women's sprinting on Sunday when she won the first major 100 metres title of her career by the width of her vest on the second day of the world championships.
The 21-year-old former basketball player had to wait for a photo-finish before she could celebrate a victory of just two-hundreths of a second over Ukraine's Zhanna Pintussevich.
The finish was so tight that Pintussevich set off on a lap of honour after the race thinking she had won, leaving Jones at the end of the straight waiting for the photo.
It was only when the scoreboard showed the result that Jones knew she had won in 10.83 seconds with the Ukrainian second in 10.85. Sevatheda Fynes of the Bahamas took the bronze medal in 11.03.
Jamaican veteran Ottey, who has won a record 13 world titles but never a 100 gold, finished seventh.
The 37-year-old's chances were adversely affected when she did not hear the gun for a false start and ran 50 metres down the track before returning slowly to her blocks.
